deliveries.title: Merge payment reconciliation concurrency protection (#632)
deliveries.declaredScopeAndLimits:
## Problem
A delayed provider GET could overwrite a payment transition committed by another request while the GET was in flight. This affected checkout replay, authenticated refresh and webhooks. Concurrent unchanged-state or unmatched webhook deliveries also lacked a serializable once-only receipt boundary.

## Change
Keep provider I/O outside transactions. In a serializable transaction, compare the persisted payment with the pre-GET snapshot (reference, status, timestamp, ownership and pricing), revalidate the provider binding, then write the provider payment reference, state transition and audit/receipt atomically. A changed snapshot returns PAYMENT_RECONCILIATION_STALE / 409 without marking the webhook processed; retry fetches a fresh invoice. Matched and unmatched event receipts use the same retryable transaction discipline.

## Validation
- Controlled compiled-service regressions reproduced the old behavior (10 failed / 2 passed); the fixed build passes all 53 targeted checks: 12 reconciliation, 8 idempotency and 33 webhook checks.
- Real HTTP/PostgreSQL 18.6 negative control failed on the old service: delayed checkout replay returned 201 instead of rejecting the newer-refund conflict.
- Fixed real HTTP/PostgreSQL suite passed: delayed create/refresh/webhook all preserve REFUNDED and leave no stale provider reference; stale event remains retryable; simultaneous unchanged-state and unmatched webhook receipts each persist exactly once. Native PostgreSQL serialization retries were exercised.
- Existing pricing, provider identity/mode, outage/recovery, checkout idempotency and booking-confirmation boundaries remain covered.
- API build, correctness lint, syntax/diff checks and independent source review passed. The fixture now uses an actual persisted synthetic session rather than sessionless CI tokens.

No live payment/refund was executed; provider traffic was loopback-only. This concerns transition reconciliation and event receipts; initial invoice creation/claim is an existing separate path. Required repository gates must pass before merge.
